cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt. The LORD says, “Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land where I tell you.” (Gen 26:2) So Isaac gets a no and a yes in one breath. That's about as clear as directions get, friends, and I've followed worse ones off a recipe card.

The answer is lands. The LORD says, “For I will give all these lands to you and your offspring…” (Gen 26:3) That promise comes right alongside “…I will be with you and bless you.” Isaac gets a whole lot more than a spot to put his tent.

The answer is True. God says, “…through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed…” (Gen 26:4) He says it to Isaac right when there's a famine in the land (Gen 26:1). Isaac is one man, and God is talking about all nations. That's a big promise, friends.

The answer is that Abraham listened to God's voice. God says it's “…because Abraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.” (Gen 26:5) Abraham, Isaac's father, listened and kept what God gave him. The text puts it just that plainly.

The answer is sister. “She is my sister.” Isaac says it when the men of that place ask about his wife, Rebekah. (Gen 26:7) That's a tricky answer to give about the woman you married. The text says he was afraid to say, “She is my wife…”

The answer is that he's afraid they'll kill him for her. The text says he was afraid to say, “She is my wife…” since he thought, “The men of this place will kill me on account of Rebekah, because she is so beautiful.” (Gen 26:7) Isaac's fear is doing the talking here. I've said some silly things when I was scared too.

The answer is Isaac caressing Rebekah. Abimelech “…was surprised to see Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.” (Gen 26:8) That look from the window shows him who Rebekah is to Isaac, and he sends for Isaac and says, “So she is really your wife!” (Gen 26:9) Isaac's story just got caught by a window.

The answer is guilt. Abimelech says, “One of the people could easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.” (Gen 26:10) I think he's rattled by what could have happened. Isaac had said she was his sister, and the king did NOT take that lightly.

The answer is True. Abimelech warns all the people, “Whoever harms this man or his wife will surely be put to death.” (Gen 26:11) Isaac was afraid of being killed, and now the king himself has said no one touches him or Rebekah. That's a pretty big turn.

The answer is that he gets richer and richer. The text says “…he became richer and richer, until he was exceedingly wealthy.” (Gen 26:13) That comes right after the LORD blessed him. Isaac keeps going up and up.

The answer is False. The text says Isaac owned so many flocks, herds and servants “…that the Philistines envied him.” (Gen 26:14) Envy is a long way from being happy for someone. And you can see where it leads in the next verse.

The answer is that they stop them up with dirt. “…the Philistines took dirt and stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham.” (Gen 26:15) Those wells went back to Abraham, Isaac's father. Dirt was the tool, and it was all of the wells. That's a LOT of shoveling, and I've done my share of digging out of a drawer, so I respect the effort.

The answer is True. Abimelech tells Isaac, “Depart from us, for you are much too powerful for us.” (Gen 26:16) That's the king talking, the same king who said no one should touch Isaac. Now he wants Isaac gone.
The answer is False. Isaac “…gave these wells the same names his father had given them.” (Gen 26:18) Same wells, same names. Abraham's names stay.

The answer is the herdsmen of Gerar. Isaac's servants had found a well of fresh water in the valley (Gen 26:19). Then Gerar's herdsmen quarrel with Isaac's herdsmen and say, “The water is ours!” (Gen 26:20) Isaac named the well Esek, because they contended with him. Somebody found water and somebody else filed a claim. I've seen that kind of thing over a parking spot.
The answer is False. The text says they “…dug another well and quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.” (Gen 26:21) Two wells, two quarrels. Peace comes at the next one.

The answer is that the LORD made room for them. Isaac names the well Rehoboth and says, “At last the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.” (Gen 26:22) After two quarrels, nobody fights over this one. I think you can hear the relief.
The answer is be afraid. The LORD says, “Do not be afraid, for I am with you.” (Gen 26:24) He gives Isaac the command and the reason in one line. That's a good one to hang on a kitchen wall, friends.

The answer is multiply. The LORD says, “I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham.” (Gen 26:24) It's Isaac's blessing, and Abraham's name is in it too. More descendants, as promised.

The answer is an altar. “So Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD…” (Gen 26:25) The LORD appears to him that night in verse 24, and the altar comes in verse 25. After that Isaac pitches his tent, and his servants dig a well.
The answer is that they hated him and sent him away. Isaac asks, “You hated me and sent me away.” (Gen 26:27) He doesn't wait around to say it. I think that line has some sting to it.

The answer is an oath that he won't harm them. They say, “We recommend that there should now be an oath between us and you.” Then they add, “…that you will not harm us, just as we have not harmed you…” (Gen 26:28-29) They say they can plainly see the LORD has been with Isaac.

The answer is True. “On that same day, Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug.” (Gen 26:32) They tell him, “We have found water!” Isaac's guests had just left him in peace (Gen 26:31). Peace and water in one day is a good day, friends.

The answer is grief. The text says, “…they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.” (Gen 26:35) Esau, Isaac's son, married Judith and Basemath at forty. It's a quiet, heavy note at the end of the chapter. And the story isn't over, friends.
